newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber close limit up on rising cash markets.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber close limit up on rising cash markets.

text.p: Rising cash lumber prices and reports of increased mill business sparked buying and buy stops were hit, buoying CME lumber futures up the daily limit at the close, traders said.

January closed limit up at $409.30 per thousand board feet and March was limit up at $395.30. May was also up the daily limit while other months were up $6.80 to $9.50 with distant September and November setting new contract highs.

Demand from the start was sparked by higher cash. Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $394, up $16 from last week, and private cash sources said spruce was now trading in the $400 area with mill asking prices up to $410.
"Cash (trade) got quite busy late in the afternoon on Tuesday, after the futures had closed, and continued busy this morning," said Curt Cunningham, president of Pacific Futures Trading.

Cash business increased after the Thanksgiving holiday and there was short covering by wholesalers, partly on ideas that mills will be announcing their upcoming holiday "down time". Many mills close during the long holiday period, traders said.
Traders also noted that charts turned bullish and locals were caught short, adding to the advance.
Further gains are seen Thursday as options on January were quoted synthetically $7 higher, pit sources said.
